sections.content: Virginia Beach, Virginia is more than a vacation destination. It is a thriving coastal city with a population of nearly 460,000 people, a massive military presence, and a housing market that has held strong through economic ups and downs. For real estate investors, that combination creates genuine opportunity across multiple deal types — from wholesale flips to long-term rentals. Whether you are brand new to investing or an experienced operator scouting your next market, this guide covers everything you need to know about finding real estate deals in Virginia Beach VA. If you are just getting started, it also helps to review the fundamentals at our Real Estate Investing for Beginners guide before diving into a specific market.
Virginia Beach Market Overview: Why Investors Are Paying Attention

Virginia Beach is consistently ranked among the largest cities on the East Coast by land area, and it has one of the most diverse economic bases in the region. The city is home to Naval Station Norfolk — the largest naval station in the world — along with Joint Expeditionary Base Little Creek-Fort Story and several other installations. That military backbone creates year-round rental demand that most coastal markets simply do not have. When tourist season ends, thousands of active-duty service members, contractors, and civilian employees keep the local economy humming.

As of mid-2024, the median home price in Virginia Beach sits around $330,000 to $350,000, with values up roughly 5 to 8 percent year-over-year depending on the neighborhood. Days on market have ticked up slightly from the pandemic-era lows, which is actually good news for buyers and investors. More time on market means more room to negotiate, and distressed sellers are starting to re-emerge after a period where nearly every home sold instantly at full price.
Best Neighborhoods for Real Estate Investors in Virginia Beach

Not all parts of Virginia Beach perform the same for investors. The city is geographically large and economically varied, so picking the right zip code matters more here than in a compact urban market. Here are the areas that consistently show up on investor radar.
Oceanfront and Resort Area (23451, 23454)

The strip along Atlantic Avenue and the surrounding blocks offer strong short-term rental income, especially from Memorial Day through Labor Day. Median prices here run higher — often $400,000 to $600,000 for condos and single-family homes — but gross rental yields on Airbnb-style properties can hit 8 to 12 percent annually for well-managed units. Investors need to stay current on city short-term rental regulations, which have tightened in recent years.

Bayside is the sweet spot for buy-and-hold investors chasing cash flow. Median prices in the $250,000 to $310,000 range make entry more accessible, and the renter population here is dense thanks to proximity to military bases and employment centers. Properties in this area also tend to attract long-term military tenants, which reduces turnover costs significantly.
Kempsville and Great Neck (23462, 23452)

These inland neighborhoods offer solid appreciation potential and appeal to families, which means lower vacancy rates for landlords. Kempsville in particular has older housing stock — a lot of it built in the 1970s and 1980s — which creates fix-and-flip opportunities for investors willing to do cosmetic and mechanical updates.
Types of Real Estate Deals Available in Virginia Beach
Wholesale Deals

Wholesaling is active in Virginia Beach, particularly in the Bayside, Kempsville, and Oceanview corridors. Motivated sellers here include military families facing sudden PCS orders (permanent change of station), estate sales from an aging population, and landlords who accumulated properties during the boom years and are now looking to exit. Learning how to find off-market real estate deals is the key skill set for wholesalers in this market, since the best opportunities rarely hit the MLS. For a deeper dive into the strategy itself, check out our guide on wholesaling real estate for beginners.
Fix and Flip

The fix-and-flip market in Virginia Beach is competitive but not oversaturated. Successful flips typically target homes in the $200,000 to $280,000 purchase range with ARVs in the $330,000 to $420,000 range after renovation. That spread leaves room for profit when rehab budgets stay controlled. The 70 percent rule is a reliable starting point: offer no more than 70 percent of ARV minus estimated repair costs. Use our free ARV Calculator to quickly estimate after-repair value before making an offer.
Long-Term Rentals

Long-term rentals are arguably the most reliable play in Virginia Beach. Average monthly rents for a 3-bedroom single-family home run between $1,800 and $2,400 depending on location and condition. With median purchase prices around $300,000, investors can realistically target a gross rent multiplier of 12 to 16, which compares favorably to other coastal Virginia markets like Richmond or Charlottesville.

Pro Tip: Military families often prefer 12-month leases with renewal options tied to their orders. If you own rental property near a base, marketing directly to the military relocation office or listing on MilitaryByOwner.com can dramatically cut vacancy time and attract highly reliable tenants.
Local Market Trends Shaping Deal Opportunities

items: Interest rate sensitivity: Higher rates have cooled buyer demand, creating more negotiating room for cash investors and those with hard money financing.
Inventory still below historical norms: Total active listings in Virginia Beach remain 20 to 30 percent below pre-2020 levels, keeping prices supported even as demand softens.
Short-term rental regulation: The city has introduced permit requirements and zoning restrictions for STRs. Investors should verify current rules before assuming Airbnb income projections.
Infrastructure investment: The city is actively investing in flood mitigation and stormwater projects, which is improving the long-term livability and value of flood-prone neighborhoods.
Remote worker migration: Virginia Beach continues to attract remote workers from Northern Virginia and DC who want more space and lower cost of living, sustaining demand in suburban zip codes.
Aging housing stock: A large percentage of homes were built between 1960 and 1985, creating a steady pipeline of properties needing updates — good news for flippers and wholesalers.

Practical Tips for Out-of-State Investors
Virginia Beach is an attractive market for remote investors, but it requires a local team to execute well. Here is how to build your presence without being physically there every week.

items: Find a local investor-friendly real estate agent: Not all agents understand investment math. Look for agents who work with landlords and flippers and can run a proper cash-on-cash analysis, not just a neighborhood comp sheet.

Build a property management relationship early: Before you close your first deal, have a property manager lined up. Virginia Beach PM fees typically run 8 to 10 percent of monthly rent for single-family homes.
Use data before you fly out: Run your numbers remotely first using tools like our free Wholesale Deal Calculator so you only visit deals that already pencil out on paper.

Understand the flood zone map: FEMA flood zones are a real consideration in coastal Virginia Beach. Flood insurance can add $1,500 to $4,000 or more annually to your holding costs — always check the flood zone before making an offer.
Join a local REIA: The Hampton Roads Real Estate Investors Association (HREIA) is active and holds regular meetups. One conversation with a local investor can save you months of research.
Know your deal analysis cold: Remote investing has zero margin for sloppy underwriting. Learn how to analyze real estate deals like a pro before you make your first offer in this or any market.

sections.content: What to Offer: A Quick Underwriting Framework

For a typical Virginia Beach flip, start with ARV, subtract your target profit (usually 15 to 20 percent of ARV), subtract estimated rehab costs, and subtract your holding and closing costs. What remains is your maximum allowable offer (MAO). On a home with a $380,000 ARV, $60,000 in needed repairs, and $25,000 in holding and transaction costs, your MAO at a 20 percent profit target would be roughly $219,000. Anything below that is a deal worth pursuing seriously. Explore the full Virginia Beach VA market data and active deals on AIWholesail to see what properties are currently available in this range.

Pro Tip: When evaluating rentals in flood-prone zip codes like 23451 or 23456, always request the flood zone designation from the listing agent or check FEMA's Flood Map Service Center before building your offer. A Zone AE designation can add significant insurance costs that will wreck an otherwise solid cash flow projection.
Is Virginia Beach Right for Your Investment Strategy?

Virginia Beach is not a get-rich-quick market. Appreciation here is steady, not explosive, and cash flow requires disciplined buying and operating. But for investors who value stability, consistent rental demand, and a market backed by genuine economic fundamentals — not speculative hype — it checks a lot of boxes. The military-driven economy, growing remote worker population, and aging housing stock all point to continued opportunity for wholesalers, flippers, and landlords willing to do the work.
